hypothesis: With the 32x64x64 blocking and scalar 4x4 register microkernel held constant, parallelizing whole row bands rather than a flattened row/column tile loop may reduce tile-index arithmetic and scheduling work. At n=1024, static flattened scheduling already gives contiguous groups, so any gain may be small; limiting workers by row-band count may also reduce parallelism on smaller sizes. The candidate remains unmeasured.
notes: The catalog reports three distinct valid programs: simple blocking, packing, and flattened-tile parallelism. This candidate tests explicit row-band ownership without packing or target-specific SIMD. Prior measurements are not results for this proposal; correctness and performance remain for controller evaluation.
transformations: Replace size-specific matrix-multiply branches with a generic n path and bounds-safe edge handling.
Use 32x64 output blocks and 64-element reduction blocks with a scalar 4x4 output microkernel.

Assign each 32-row band, including all its column blocks, to one static OpenMP loop iteration; cap workers by both the caller thread count and row-band count, with serial execution when OpenMP is unavailable or one worker is requested.
Initialize accumulators to zero on the first reduction block and store all output elements on every call, without a separate C initialization pass.
